item.title: Tuesday Morning, Oct 20
item.description:
The Tuesday morning bulletin from Gumshoe News Radio for October 20, 2026: an eight-billion-dollar fuel relief program for farmers, a seven-hour hearing in the D.C. golf course fight, doubts about the promised five-thousand-dollar checks; Houthi strikes on Saudi oil and airports with British jets reportedly on the way, a Reuters report on Iran's midterm strategy, Russia's overnight barrage as Zelenskyy meets U.S. envoys in Oslo, a calmer night in Paris, and Alberta voting to stay in Canada; futures mixed as chip stocks slip again, with Netflix and SpaceX reporting tonight; Japan's launch to the moons of Mars and a Revolut outage; a federal DeepSeek ban and OpenAI's race to raise money; hijacked backup-software updates and a backdoored WordPress plugin; your X feed with dhh, Cremieux in Tokyo, and metals that shrug off extreme cold; New Hampshire's ballot-counter hearing, a Harris endorsement and Londonderry trick-or-treat hours; and a fifteen-year-old who used his CPR training to save a life. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Monday 4 PM Update, Oct 19
item.description:
The Monday four o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 19, 2026: a federal judge refusing to step aside in the D.C. golf course case after a courtroom clash with a top Justice Department official, and President Trump saying it may be time for someone other than President Zelenskyy to negotiate for Ukraine; overnight curfews in Paris, Lyon and Nice, and Israel reopening Gaza to commercial goods; Wall Street's tech-led rebound at the close; Apple's "Pro and tell" event and Europe's big carriers teaming up against Starlink; Gemini agents beating Minecraft on their own; a hacked remote-support tool tied to suspected Chinese spies, a report on a voting-machine request at CISA, and the ex-OpenAI engineer held without bail; your X feed with Richard Riehle, Jon Stewart, Saturn's ring spokes and an iPhone shortcut for Grok Bot; the nor'easter that's staying offshore and Halloween events around Londonderry; and teenagers who made a lonely seven-year-old's day. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Monday 1 PM Update, Oct 19
item.description:
The Monday one o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 19, 2026: a federal sweep of alleged noncitizen voters in California, the Supreme Court turning away the 9/11 plea-deal appeals and taking up the home-distilling ban, and the signing of the women's health executive order; France's first curfews and a blockaded Louvre, the rising toll from a Houthi strike in Yemen, Iran's claim of a U.S. strike on a naval base, and deep food-aid cuts in Gaza; a midday market rebound led by chips, with homebuilder confidence at a 14-year low; Nvidia winning Modal for its new CPUs and a shake-up at Netflix; Washington ordering DeepSeek off federal systems; a hacker who let AI agents break into more than 100 company websites, and new allegations against an ex-OpenAI engineer; your X feed with Jalen Hurts, Christiane Amanpour and a council of Claudes; Londonderry's water-line progress and tonight's council meeting; and a 99-year-old wing walker. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Monday 10 AM Update, Oct 19
item.description:
The Monday 10 AM update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 19, 2026: Florida's arrest warrant for Raúl Castro over the 1996 Brothers to the Rescue shootdown, President Trump's plan to close a historic Washington golf course, and a new poll of Asian American voters; France weighing a state of emergency after weekend riots, hoax bomb threats emailed to hundreds of schools in Northern Ireland and Scotland, and arrests over settler attacks in the West Bank; tech stocks rebounding at the open, led by Intel and CoreWeave; Disney hiring most of Character.AI's staff; MiniMax's low-cost M3.1 Flash model; fake crypto-accelerator npm packages that hijack AI coding agents; your X feed with a drone medevac in Ukraine, Chinese EVs and an iPhone motion-sickness trick; the data center backlash in New England and Londonderry events; and a Massachusetts teen's comfort kits for kids in the hospital. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.
